summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, multiple pulmonary emboli, and recent pneumonia was admitted after a fall with elevated creatine kinase, indicating rhabdomyolysis. She developed acute kidney injury, hyponatremia, and weakness. Workup revealed a new pulmonary embolism, urinary tract infection, and persistent pneumonia. She was treated with IV fluids, antibiotics, anticoagulation, and supportive care. A muscle biopsy was performed to evaluate for toxic myopathy. Her condition improved over 18 days, with resolution of infection, stabilization of kidney function, and gradual strength recovery. She was discharged home on supplemental oxygen with plans for follow-up and outpatient management of her muscle disorder.
